title: Measure response
description: Response from POST /measure. One entry per scale-recovery arm (ARCHITECTURE.md section 5). Frozen by TICK-060 before any metrology exists, so client rendering (TICK-063) and the library (TICK-043 onward) proceed in parallel; TICK-061 fills real values in behind this identical shape. Two cross-field constraints on arm_result cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are enforced by validate_measure_response() in frontdoor_server/app.py: the interval must not be inverted, and rise_in must lie inside it. Validating against this schema alone is therefore not sufficient (TICK-223).

stub.description: True while the endpoint returns fixed placeholder values instead of measurements. TICK-061 sets it false. Clients must surface it, so stub output is never mistaken for a measurement.

capture_id.description: Echoed from the request sidecar, so a response is always tied back to the capture it came from.

arms.description: Keyed by arm name from the metrology registry (TICK-040). All four keys are required, and each is either a result or an explicit absence — so a client is never left to guess whether a missing arm was cut, failed, or is unavailable here (TICK-222).

arm.description: One arm is either a measurement or a stated absence, never nothing at all. Discriminated on absent_reason rather than expressed as a bare oneOf, so a malformed arm reports the field that is actually wrong instead of 'not valid under any of the given schemas'.

arm_result.description: One arm's answer for one capture: a measurement, its interval, and a decision per ADA line.

rise_in.description: Threshold rise in inches. Always present, including when a decision is abstain. Cannot be negative — a threshold does not rise by less than nothing. Deliberately has no upper bound: an implausibly large rise is a measurement error for TICK-207 to surface, and capping it here would turn a visible bad number into a contract failure. Must lie within interval_in; that is enforced in code, not here.

arm_absent.description: This arm produced no measurement, and says why. TICK-063 renders the three reasons differently: a cut arm is expected, a failed arm is about this capture, an unavailable arm is about this deployment.

absent_reason.description: cut — dropped by a project decision, e.g. Arm C on 2026-09-02 per D-013. failed — this arm could not measure this capture. unavailable — this arm is not served by this deployment, e.g. a free-tier host with no room for the depth model (TICK-062).

detail.description: Optional human-readable specifics. Must contain a non-whitespace character, for the same reason explanation must. The reason is what a client branches on; this is what it shows.

interval.description: Confidence interval on rise_in, in inches. Method settled by TICK-050; the shape does not depend on which method wins. low must not exceed high — enforced in code, since JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling values.

decisions.description: One decision per ADA line. The 1/2 inch line is the pre-registered primary and the 1/4 inch line the secondary (PRD.md section 2); they are computed independently, so one may abstain while the other does not.

decision.description: The verdict at one line, plus the reason when there is no verdict to give. abstain is a first-class outcome (D-009), emitted when the interval straddles the line — never a missing or null measurement, and never a blank on screen.

verdict.description: pass — the rise clears this line. fail — it exceeds it. abstain — the interval straddles it and no honest verdict exists.

explanation.description: Why this verdict, in a sentence a client can render as-is. REQUIRED when verdict is abstain, so an abstention can never render blank (TICK-211 AC4); optional otherwise, since pass and fail are self-explanatory beside the number. Constrained by pattern rather than minLength because a whitespace-only string satisfies minLength and still renders as a blank, which is the failure this field exists to prevent.
